business_problem: Databento needed to deliver institutional market data with very low latency over the internet, but legacy finance networking products were expensive, fragmented, and hard to operate at the bandwidth required for hundreds of billions of updates per day.
solution_summary: Databento rebuilt its private-cloud market-data backbone on NVIDIA networking. Across four data centers and more than 30 PB of storage, the company uses NVIDIA Spectrum Ethernet switches, ConnectX SuperNICs, and Cumulus Linux so network devices can be managed with the same automation patterns as servers. For latency-sensitive packet delivery, ConnectX NICs work with DPDK and VMA to keep host-to-host forwarding deterministic, while Netris provides software-defined overlays that help the infrastructure scale elastically as traffic and storage needs grow. The result is a unified network that can serve ultra-low-latency options data to cloud customers, support preprocessing and format customization for downstream machine-learning pipelines, and avoid the cost and operational sprawl of niche proprietary market-data networking stacks.

data_flow: Exchange updates enter Databento's private cloud, traverse Spectrum switches and ConnectX NICs with DPDK acceleration, are customized and serialized for client APIs and ML workflows, and then are delivered over the internet with deterministic latency from the four-data-center backbone.
business_outcome: Databento achieved median latency below 60 microseconds, delivered U.S. options data online in under 242 microseconds, lowered networking costs by 20%, reduced network-management effort by more than 60%, and enabled customers to avoid expensive colocation by getting very low latency over the public internet.
